content.title: Server Actions and Form Mutations
content.hook: Reading data is only half the application.
content.context:
Users also create, update, and delete things.

Next.js supports Server Actions for server-side mutations.

The key concept is simple:

**The user performs an interaction. The application invokes server-side code.**
goals: Master Server Actions and Form Mutations: The user performs an interaction. The application invokes server-side code.

content.title: Example shape
content.text:
```tsx
<form action={saveProfile}>
  <input name="name" />
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
```

The server-side action can receive the submitted form data.

content.question: What should the server ultimately decide for a protected mutation?

options.text: Whether the operation is allowed and how the data should be changed
Whether the browser button is blue
Whether the user's monitor is large enough

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. Whether the operation is allowed and how the data should be changed
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. Whether the operation is allowed and how the data should be changed

content.title: Why this matters
content.text:
A form is not merely a UI object.

It crosses a trust boundary.

The browser can submit data.

The server must validate and process that data.

Security-sensitive authorization remains a server responsibility.

content.title: Redirect and revalidation
content.text:
After a successful mutation, the application may need to:

1. update the stored data,
2. invalidate or refresh relevant cached data,
3. redirect the user or return the updated result.

The exact mechanism matters, but the higher-level sequence is what you should remember.

options.text: Client-side validation is enough for every mutation.
The server should validate and enforce important rules for mutations.
The browser should decide who is authorized.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. The server should validate and enforce important rules for mutations.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. The server should validate and enforce important rules for mutations.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Treat submitted data as untrusted input until the server validates it.
nextSteps: Write the steps for a profile-update flow from button press to successful completion. Identify where browser behavior ends and server enforcement begins.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
